title: PartyConfig
description: Customer/party-level master data from the host system's Customer Payload (e.g. C4C) — territory, customer country/currency, and the customer's own Origin of Data. Deliberately distinct from an item's own `ood`: the two can diverge on a single order (e.g. a US customer, ood SMA, ordering a part whose cost data originates in China) — item-level ood keeps driving cost-route branching (see region-config's China build-up), while customerOod here drives region-route resolution. One customerId = one versioned, effective-dated document, independent of region/salesOrg — a customer's master data doesn't change depending on who priced them. First real consumer of the `party.customerId` field the object-agnostic request has carried since Phase 1 (requirements §7) but nothing previously read.

customerOod.description: The customer's own Origin of Data — feeds region-route resolution when a pricing request omits `region` explicitly.

tier.description: Commercial tier (e.g. "A", "B") — a price-list / catalog dimension: rows and discounts may match on it (ARCHITECTURE_V2 §2.6). srv copies it onto request.party.tier before pricing.

segment.description: Industry segment (e.g. "IND" industrial, "AUT" automotive, "AER" aerospace) — a second price-list / catalog dimension alongside tier, for rows that vary by the customer's industry rather than (or in addition to) their commercial tier. srv copies it onto request.party.segment before pricing.
